dedupe_keys.name: data set of ionospheric scintillation in low latitude gnss radio occultation measurements

description: This dataset contains features of labelled GNSS radio occultation measurements at low latitudes, each marked as ionospheric scintillation (label 1) or other disturbance (label 0). It was published in April 2021 by Vinícius Ludwig-Barbosa at the Blekinge Institute of Technology to train and test a support vector machine that classifies unlabelled occultation measurements, as described in the paper Supervised Detection of Ionospheric Scintillation in Low-Latitude Radio Occultation Measurements (Remote Sensing, 2021). The keywords point to Metop radio occultation data. Coverage is the low-latitude band where equatorial scintillation is strongest. Format and access: one ZIP archive of about 738 MB on Zenodo, downloadable without login. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: it is a training set of extracted features, not raw signals, and its labels follow the authors' selection rules. It supports hazard exposure work on GNSS signal degradation by space weather, for example validating scintillation detectors. Related catalogue records are the GNSS SDR signals subject to ionospheric scintillations and the CPSSM scintillation simulator.
